newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy centrist party elects new secretary.
newsitem.headline: Italy centrist party elects new secretary.

text.p: Franco Marini was elected on Sunday as new secretary of the small Italian Popular Party (PPI), one of the successors of the defunct Christian Democrats.
Marini, a former union leader, was elected after outgoing leader Gerardo Bianco decided not to run for re-election during a weekend party congress.

The centrist party, which is part of Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left coalition, is one of the various groupings that emerged after the Christian Democrats were swallowed up by corruption scandals in the early 1990s.
The PPI groups politicians who were once members of the Christian Democrats' left-leaning wing.
Marini defeated Pierluigi Castagnetti, who appealed for party unity after his defeat.
